_comment: The car domain's criteria — decisions 5–11 of docs/plans/archive/scout-rename-and-car-domain.plan.md. ONE hard ceiling (the displayed price), a geography filter that acts only on a STATED location, and score components for everything else. A gitignored criteria.local.json beside this file overrides field by field. Unknown keys are refused.
_max_price_eur: Decision 5: 0–30 000 € on the DISPLAYED price — wide on purpose, the score discriminates.
_postcode_prefixes: Decision 6, revisited. EMPTY = national, and that is the honest state rather than a widening (Track 1c). It was the eight Île-de-France departements, copied from the rent side — and it was INERT: no car source maps a postcode at all, so `matchesLocation()` was answering true for every vehicle regardless. Leaving the list in place meant the filter would activate silently and asymmetrically the day a source first mapped one, on criteria nobody had reconsidered for cars. A car is driven to you; the geography that matters is the seller's, and no source publishes it yet. Reversed by restoring the eight prefixes in this one line.
_body_favour: Was `body_rank` until Track 7 (developer ruling 2026-09-08: *suv, break, berline — very high score*). Decision 11 made it a RANK on the commune_rank mechanism, so `suv` took the whole share, `break` two thirds and `berline` one third. The three are now EQUAL, which leaves the position meaning nothing — hence the rename, because a key whose name asserts a mechanism that no longer exists is the failure this repo has paid for most often. THE LIST IS UNCHANGED; only the key and the arithmetic moved. `4x4 - suv` (60 stored cars) still reads as suv, because the match is `str_contains`. An unlisted body still scores 0 and is still NOTIFIED — a preference, never a disqualifier. The loader refuses `body_rank` by name and says what to write. Reversed by restoring the positional share in VehicleScorer.
_peak_age_years: Decision 7: ≤ 5 years and ≤ 80 000 km are SCORE PEAKS, never disqualifiers; the portal saved searches are set wider (7 y / 100 000 km) so near-misses arrive and are ranked.
_weights: Sum to 100. price: lower is better, linear from the ceiling. age/mileage: full marks up to the peak, 0 at twice it. gearbox: automatic (decision 11) — at weight 0 since Track 7, so it scores nothing either way. fuel: petrol/hybrid/electric over diesel — a PREFERENCE, never a ZFE claim, and a diesel still appears. body: FLAT since Track 7 — a listed body takes the whole share, see _body_favour; it was a rank. brand: a THREE-WAY since Track 7 — favoured takes it all, avoided and unlisted take none; it was an INVERTED rank. See _brand_avoid and _brand_favour. TWO REBALANCES, both keeping the total at 100 because `high_priority_score` is an ABSOLUTE threshold and a scale that shifts silently changes what the marker means. (1) 2026-08-31: brand's 10 points came from price (25→20) and body (15→10) — a DEFAULT APPLIED, not a ruling; what was ruled is only that brand comes out of the 100. (2) 2026-09-01, DEVELOPER RULING: fuel 10→20, taken 5 from price and 5 from mileage, because diesels were ranking high enough to be noticed. MEASURED over all 269 judged snapshots rather than predicted: the diesel/clean median gap goes 16→25, the best diesel 77→70, and the diesels reaching the clean median 5→1, while ordering among the cars actually wanted is PRESERVED (clean-car spread 23→24). −5/−5 rather than −10 from price on purpose: price is the largest factor for a used car and halving it as a side effect of a fuel decision is a bigger change than the decision. fuel 30 was measured and REJECTED — it compresses the clean-car spread to 21 and marks 64%% of pushes, which is where the cure starts costing more than the complaint. --- THIRD REBALANCE, developer ruling 2026-09-08 — SPLIT B, and it is the only measured split that separates cleanly. All 951 stored car MATCHes were re-judged through the REAL scorer, each component isolated exactly (weight 100 on one, 0 on the rest), then recombined under five candidate splits. At the EXISTING gate of 73, B gives 197 individual pushes and EVERY ONE of them is a favoured make: zero avoided, zero unlisted, zero unknown-make. Split A left 26 avoided cars above the gate, split D 104, split C (unlisted at half share) pushed 16 of the 47 unlisted. That is the ruling *everything else must almost not show up* satisfied by CALIBRATION rather than by a new mechanism — the rest still reaches the developer once a day through `scout --domain=car rollup`. GEARBOX GOES TO 0, which is how *accept both manual and automatic* was implemented: 276 of 1 004 stored cars state NO gearbox, so awarding both arms full marks would still have scored 0 for 27 % of the fleet on a fact that no longer discriminates — a penalty for silence, hard rule 9's own shape. At weight 0 the component drops out and its 10 points fund body and brand. FUEL DROPS 20 → 15, partially reversing the 2026-09-01 ruling, and that was MEASURED rather than re-argued: over the same 951 rows B puts 15 of 245 diesels above gate 73 where the current weights put 0, and every one of the fifteen is a favoured-make suv/break/berline arriving through the front door of the two rules this track adds. Both alternatives were measured in the same run and rejected — fuel 20 with price → 5 removes only 2 of the 15 (the diesels ride body 25 + brand 25, not the fuel weight), and fuel 20 with age → 10 removes 12 only by halving the second-heaviest signal on a used-car list. The diesel/clean median gap goes 27 → 20 and 91 % of individual pushes are still petrol, hybrid or electric; the fuel preference was never a disqualifier and must not become one. `high_priority_score` and `push_min_score` were both RE-MEASURED under these weights and both STAY at 73 — but the selectivity moved and saying so is the point: 73 now marks 197 of 951 judged MATCHes, **20.7 %**, where the 2026-09-01 calibration put it at 27.1 % of the 269 then stored. The threshold is unchanged because what it selects is now exactly the population the developer asked for (every one of the 197 a favoured make), not because the number happened to survive; a bar that keeps its old selectivity would have had to move DOWN, admitting avoided makes back.
_brand_avoid: Developer ruling 2026-08-31: a PENALTY, not a preference ranking. Deliberately NOT named `brand_rank` — the body list's mechanism scored its TOP entry highest, which here would have rewarded exactly the makes being avoided. A listed make earns none of the `brand` weight; no ordering among them was ruled, so they are equal. Folded at load, so the config may write `Peugeot` and a payload `PEUGEOT`. TWO SENTENCES THAT STOOD HERE ARE NOW WRONG AND ARE CORRECTED RATHER THAN DELETED, because both were load-bearing for a reader. (1) *'An unlisted make earns the whole brand weight'* — true until Track 7, and the ruling of 2026-09-08 is the opposite: with `brand_favour` configured an unlisted make earns NOTHING, which is what *everything else must have lowest score* asks for. Only when BOTH lists are empty does every make earn the share, and that arm is what keeps the achievable maximum at 100 for a deployment configuring no preference at all. (2) *'A make that could not be extracted earns the full share too (hard rule 9)'* — this was NEVER true of the shipped code: `VehicleScorer`'s null-make arm scores 0 and says `marque inconnue — hors score`, a deliberate deviation made because awarding the share would rank an EXTRACTION FAILURE as a definitely-not-Peugeot. The same claim sat in that method's own docblock and was refuted fifteen lines below it; an audit finding (Track 6-A4 N3) reasoned from it and recommended a fix for a problem that did not exist. FORD LEFT THIS LIST on 2026-09-08 and is on `brand_favour` now — see there for the measurement.
_why: brand_avoid, two things about it. FIRST, EACH ENTRY IS A STEM, matched to a non-letter boundary — never an exact string. Measured 2026-09-01: the live store holds the same marque as `ds` (leboncoin) and `ds automobiles` (autohero), and exact equality caught one and silently missed the other. So write the SHORTEST unambiguous form — `alfa`, not `alfa romeo`; `fiat` also covers `fiat professional` — because the gap runs both ways and a stem longer than the make misses just as quietly. SECOND, the 22 ruled 2026-09-01 are NOT 'Stellantis' — do not tidy the list into one. Stellantis contributes 14 marques (peugeot citroen ds opel vauxhall fiat abarth lancia alfa jeep dodge chrysler ram maserati); ford and chevrolet are the developer's own additions and belong to neither group; renault, dacia, nissan, alpine and mitsubishi are the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi alliance, in because they share Renault mechanicals (Dacia is a rebadge, the Nissan 1.2 DIG-T is the Renault H5Ft, the European Colt is a Clio); leapmotor is Stellantis-distributed rather than a Stellantis marque. Reversed make by make in the one line below.
_brand_favour: The FAVOURED half of Track 7's three-way (developer ruling 2026-09-08: *for brands I want it also high score*). SAME STEM SEMANTICS AS `brand_avoid` and the same matcher, deliberately — the `ds` / `ds automobiles` miss that forced the non-letter boundary runs in BOTH directions, and a favoured list compared by exact equality would silently miss one source's spelling while every score stayed plausible. So `mercedes` covers `mercedes-benz`, and each entry is the SHORTEST unambiguous form. Fifteen makes were named by the developer; the sixteenth is FORD, MOVED HERE FROM `brand_avoid` on a measurement rather than an argument: under these weights ford's 28 stored cars score median 80 / max 95 with 17 of 28 clearing the gate if favoured, and median 55 / max 70 with 0 of 28 if avoided — the stock is Puma, Kuga, Focus, EcoSport, petrol and mild-hybrid SUVs from 2020–2023 at €12 490–15 990, precisely the shape the body and fuel preferences reward. The deciding argument is that `_why` above already admits ford belonged to NEITHER group it justifies: Stellantis contributes 14 marques and the Renault alliance 5, while ford and chevrolet were the developer's own additions with no group rationale — so this restates a preference rather than breaking a rule. CHEVROLET STAYS ON `brand_avoid` and the choice is moot: 0 rows in the store. A make on BOTH lists is refused at load. Reversed make by make in the one line below.
_exclude_patterns: Extra exclusions over the folded text, beside the non-configurable §1 vehicle set in VehicleClassifier. Empty on purpose: the ParuVendu alert is already 'Voiture d'occasion'.

notify._channels: Same channel names as the rent side; built by the same factory, with the [car-watch] prefix.
notify._high_priority_score: CALIBRATED against the store rather than guessed, which is what the rent side's own 70 was not — and RE-MEASURED on every change to the weights, because an absolute threshold silently changes meaning when the scale beneath it moves. 2026-09-01, after the fuel rebalance (10→20): re-judging all 269 stored snapshots through the real scorer at reference 2026-09 gives min 0, median 63, p90 79, max 89. The old 70 marked 27.9%% of them; under the new weights 73 marks 27.1%%, the closest match, so the marker keeps the selectivity it had. 78 was the first guess and was WRONG — it came from measuring the petrol/hybrid subset (where 70 marked 50%%) while the threshold applies to everything, which is this repo's own 'a true number from the wrong population' failure. Every row in the sample is a MATCH (nothing in it was ever rejected), so the sample still cannot say what a tighter bar would cost; revisit with a week of real rejections in view.
notify._push_min_score: A5 (Track 6, developer ruling 2026-09-05, the car half): a MATCH scoring below this is NOT pushed on its own — it waits for the daily ROLLUP (`scout --domain=car rollup`, and the floor at rollup_hour under --watch), which is deliberately not called a digest: the car domain has none and the rent digest means tenure doubt. MEASURED 2026-09-05 over all 646 stored MATCHes: p10 29 · p50 61 · p90 78; ≥73 → 24 %, ≥78 → 19 %. 73 is the marker's own calibrated bar (above), so about one match in four arrives individually and the rest once a day. Separate knob from high_priority_score on purpose; remove the key to push every match again.
notify._rollup_hour: Local hour of the daily rollup floor under --watch (the zone is TZ, as for the rent digest). Silent on a day with nothing queued; the marker state/car-rollup.txt is written only after the channel confirms. Remove the key to keep the verb only.
notify._source_alert_cooldown_hours: One alert per (source, status) per cooldown — the rent side's rule, same default.
